description: Make the dashboard easier to operate by adding four related UX improvements in static/app.js (and style.css/index.html as needed), all grounded in existing patterns. (c) a visible 'Clear this round' control on every round screen with the correct downstream-only cascade; (d) self-explaining disabled controls that state WHY they are disabled; (a) a prominent 'what to do next' guide on the overview; (g) one-level client-side Undo for all destructive actions. engine.py stays untouched. No third-party deps. Schema stays version 4.
steps: EXTEND the cascade in resetStage(key) so clearing round1 cascades to all later rounds. Change the mapping from `key==='round2'?['round2','final']:[key]` to also handle round1: round1 -> ['round1','round2','final'], round2 -> ['round2','final'], final -> ['final']. Keep the existing per-stage clearing logic (zeroing goals arrays to the right length, clearing extras/roster, resetting round2 draw to blank_draw-equivalent {order:[],revealed:0,completed:0,mode:'random'}, clearing round1 lineups). Verify the final/round2 cascade behavior is unchanged.

(c) CLEAR-ROUND CONTROLS: Add a visible, always-available (not only-when-stale) .danger 'Clear this round' control to each of the three round screens. For To Live (round1 branch of round() in app.js): a control labeled e.g. 'Clear To Live (also clears To Die & Rebirth)' that dispatches a new action, e.g. data-action='clear-round' data-stage='round1'. For To Die (round2Page()): 'Clear To Die (also clears Rebirth)' data-stage='round2'. For Rebirth (finalPage()): 'Clear Rebirth' data-stage='final'. Each control's copy MUST state exactly what it clears per the cascade. Place it in a clearly-labeled panel (reuse panel()/.panel and the .danger class, mirror the existing 'Start over' panel in settings()). Keep the existing stale-triggered 'reset-stage' buttons working: either converge them onto the same clear-round action (preferred: have reset-stage reuse the same handler) or leave them but ensure both paths go through the extended resetStage + undo flow. Do not remove the whole-tournament 'reset-all' control.

(c) DISPATCHER: Add a 'clear-round' case to the document click dispatcher that calls the shared destructive helper (see undo step): snapshot current state, run resetStage(stage), then changed()+save(). This REPLACES the scary confirm() for per-round clears with act-then-undo. The stage comes from b.dataset.stage. The existing 'reset-stage' action should route through the same code path (snapshot + resetStage + save) so it also gets undo.

(g) ONE-LEVEL UNDO: Add a single module-level `undoSnapshot` holding {state: <deep clone>, label: <short human string>} (null when none). Implement a helper, e.g. `function doDestructive(label, fn){ undoSnapshot={state: structuredClone(state), label}; fn(); changed(); } ` (use structuredClone with a JSON round-trip fallback for the vm/test sandbox: `const clone=o=>{try{return structuredClone(o);}catch{return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(o));}}`). Route ALL destructive actions through it so each sets the snapshot BEFORE mutating: clear-round cascade, 'clear-r2-game', 'clear-game', the reshuffle 'r1-reroll' (snapshot BEFORE the server reroll so undo restores the prior split; after the PUT returns, keep the snapshot of the pre-reroll state), and 'reset-all'. Taking any new destructive action REPLACES the snapshot (only one level). For the reshuffle, snapshot before calling rerollRound1Game and have undo restore+persist via the normal save path.

(g) UNDO AFFORDANCE: Render an obvious, consistent 'Undo' affordance near the footer #save-status area whenever undoSnapshot is set. Add markup in static/index.html (an element next to #save-status, e.g. a hidden <button id='undo-action'> with a label span) OR inject it from render(); keep it consistent across screens. Clicking Undo restores `state=undoSnapshot.state`, clears undoSnapshot, then changed()+save() so the restore persists through PUT /api/state with the current revision. After a successful save/render the affordance shows the label (e.g. 'Undo: Clear To Live') and hides when undoSnapshot is null. Wire the click either via the existing document click dispatcher (data-action='undo') or a dedicated $('#undo-action').onclick handler following the #retry-save pattern. Ensure undo survives a save round-trip: restoring then saving writes the prior state back; confirm the server echo repopulates state/view/revision.

(d) SELF-EXPLAINING DISABLED CONTROLS: Audit every disabled primary/submit/draw/reshuffle button across the stage screens and the wheel and attach a short visible reason derived from view.<stage>.issues or the specific precondition. Concretely: (i) To Live/Rebirth 'Submit Match N' (matchSubmit): when disabled, show a .hint/.notice next to it explaining why ('Enter a score for every player in Game N first' when the match is not ready, or 'Finish every match first' when it is the last match and not all ready, or the stage's stale issue). (ii) To Live 'Reshuffle teams' (r1-reroll): when disabled because the game is scored, show 'This game already has scores. Clear them before reshuffling.' (iii) To Die 'Draw Match 1 sit-outs' / 'Match N done' and the match selector tabs: when disabled, explain ('Finish To Live and resolve cut ties first', 'Enter the six scheduled scores for Game N first', 'Finish Match N before opening the next'). (iv) Rebirth 'Mark win': when disabled due to stale, explain. (v) The wheel SPIN button when names list is empty: 'Add at least one name to spin.' Make primary action labels explicit about what they do (e.g. keep 'Submit Match N of X' explicit). Use the existing notice()/.hint/.notice patterns and/or title/aria-label; do not introduce silent no-ops. Where issues already surface via notice(view.issues) at the top, additionally attach the specific reason adjacent to the disabled control so the user sees it in context.

(a) NEXT-STEP GUIDE: In overview(), surface the existing `next` computation as a prominent friendly banner/callout at the top of the leaderboard screen that names the next CONCRETE action and includes a button linking straight to that screen (reuse data-tab='<next>' so the existing dispatcher opens it). Drive the wording off the current stage's first unmet issue / readiness so it stays accurate as the tournament progresses. Suggested mapping: next==='settings' -> 'Start here: enter 10 unique player names' (button 'Open Players & rules'); next==='round1' -> use view.round1.issues[0] or 'Score the five To Live games, then submit' (button 'Open To Live'); next==='round2' -> if To Live tie exists say 'Resolve the To Live tie (extra games) before To Die', else view.round2.issues[0] or 'Draw sit-outs and play the eight To Die matches' (button 'Open To Die'); next==='final' and final incomplete -> view.final.issues[0] or 'Play the ten Rebirth games to decide the podium' (button 'Open Rebirth'); when the whole tournament is complete -> a celebratory 'Tournament complete. Review the podium below.' Reuse .notice / .accent / .round-path styling and keep the control-room look. Keep the existing .round-path accent indicator.

Reconcile confirm() dialogs: remove the per-round/per-game/reshuffle confirm() calls in favor of act-then-undo (they now set a snapshot and show Undo). You MAY keep a single lightweight confirm() on the whole-tournament 'reset-all' at your discretion, but reset-all MUST also set the undo snapshot so it can be undone. The wheel 'wheel-clear'/'wheel-roster' confirms may stay as-is (not in scope for undo), but do not break them.

Add/adjust CSS in static/style.css for any new elements (undo affordance button near the footer, the next-step banner) reusing existing color variables and the .danger/.accent/.notice/.hint look. Keep reducedMotion() respected for any transitions.

Update README.md briefly to document: the per-round 'Clear this round' controls and their exact downstream cascade; that disabled controls now explain themselves; the 'what to do next' guide on the Leaderboard; and the one-level Undo for destructive actions.

Run both test suites locally while iterating; keep them green. (New assertions are added in FEAT-003.) Commit the implementation on feat/per-match-ranking with a clear conventional-commit message (e.g. 'feat: clear-round controls, self-explaining disabled buttons, next-step guide, one-level undo'). Do NOT push.
acceptance_criteria: resetStage('round1') zeroes round1, round2, and final player goals (and round1 lineups, round2 draw, final results, and all three extras/rosters); resetStage('round2') clears round2+final only; resetStage('final') clears final only; earlier rounds are never touched.
Each of To Live, To Die, and Rebirth renders a visible .danger 'Clear this round' control available regardless of stale state, with copy stating exactly which rounds it clears.

Triggering a clear-round / clear-r2-game / clear-game / reshuffle / reset-all sets a one-level undo snapshot and shows an obvious Undo affordance near #save-status; clicking Undo restores the exact prior state and persists it through PUT /api/state; taking a second destructive action replaces the snapshot.

Every disabled primary/submit/draw/reshuffle button has an adjacent human-readable reason (via .hint/.notice or title/aria) explaining why it is disabled, derived from view.<stage>.issues or the specific precondition. No silent no-ops.

The Leaderboard shows a prominent next-step banner that names the next concrete action and has a button linking to the relevant screen, with wording that reflects the current `next` value and the stage's first unmet issue.
engine.py is unchanged; state schema stays version 4; no third-party dependencies added.
`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` and `node tests/test_ui.cjs` both stay green.
findings:
Implemented all four sub-features in static/app.js plus static/index.html, static/style.css, and README.md. engine.py untouched; schema stays version 4; no deps added. Both suites green (33 Python unittests OK, node tests/test_ui.cjs exit 0) and python3 -c 'import engine, app' OK.

Key decisions / notes for later features (FEAT-003 adds test assertions):
- resetStage cascade extended via resetCascade(key): round1 -> [round1,round2,final], round2 -> [round2,final], final -> [final].
- Clear-round controls: clearRoundPanel(key) renders a visible .danger panel on every round screen (To Live/To Die/Rebirth), always available, with exact-cascade copy. data-action='clear-round' data-stage=<key>. The old stale-only reset-stage buttons were replaced by a notice() + the always-available panel; the 'reset-stage' action still routes through the same clear-round code path so any lingering reference stays undoable.
- Undo: module-level undoSnapshot={state:clone(state),label}; clone() uses structuredClone with JSON fallback for the vm sandbox. doDestructive(label,fn) snapshots BEFORE mutating. #undo-action button added in index.html near #save-status (wired like #retry-save). render()/renderRoom() call renderUndo().
- IMPORTANT SERVER CONSTRAINT (discovered via live probe): app.py store.save() rejects a PUT whose round2.draw differs from the stored draw UNLESS allow_draw/restore is set or the state is an empty reset. Undo that restores a previously-saved sit-out draw (e.g. undo of Clear To Live / Clear To Die / reset-all) would 400 on the normal save path. performUndo() therefore persists via a direct PUT /api/state with restore:true (mirrors the backup-restore handler), not changed()+save(). Verified end to end with a single-invocation live probe (clear To Live cascade persisted; undo restored exact prior state via restore:true).
- reshuffle (r1-reroll): snapshot taken BEFORE the server reroll inside rerollRound1Game and assigned to undoSnapshot after the echo returns, so undo restores the pre-reroll split.
- Self-explaining disabled controls: matchSubmit, r1-reroll, clear-r2-game, r2-done, r2 match tabs, r2-start (round2Page early return), final clear-game, final Mark win, and wheel SPIN all now carry an adjacent .hint.reason and a title/aria-disabled with a specific reason. reset-all keeps a single lightweight confirm() but also sets the undo snapshot.
- Next-step banner: nextStepBanner(next,finished) at top of overview(), reuses .notice + data-tab button; round-path .accent kept.
- CSS added at end of style.css: .next-step, .hint.reason, #undo-action, button[aria-disabled]. reducedMotion already globally guarded.
- Scratch live probe was written under /projects/sandbox (outside repo) and removed after use.

FOLLOW-UP POLISH PASS (post-review 2026-10-07-074840, three flagged non-blocking issues):
- Item 1 (UNDO RETRYABILITY): performUndo() previously nulled undoSnapshot and re-rendered BEFORE await flush()/the restore PUT, so a mid-undo failure lost the snapshot and the user could not retry. Fixed in static/app.js: capture const snap=undoSnapshot (prior=snap.state), do flush()+PUT inside a try, clear undoSnapshot=null only AFTER the restore persists, and in catch restore undoSnapshot=snap + renderUndo() (so the Undo button reappears) before re-throwing. Success behavior unchanged (adopts server echo of state/view/revision, shows 'Undo applied'). The restore:true PUT shape is unchanged.
- Item 3 (DEAD reset-stage ALIAS): CHOSE TO REMOVE the dead branch. No button emits data-action='reset-stage' anymore (stale-only buttons became notices routed through clear-round), so the dispatcher now branches on action==='clear-round' only. This keeps the dispatcher honest with no behavior change.
- Both suites stay green after the pass (33 Python unittests OK, node tests/test_ui.cjs exit 0) and bash /projects/sandbox/probe_easier.sh prints PROBE OK (exit 0).
